walkthroughs.body_html:
Handling Data — a core area of GCSE Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Handling Data brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Handling Data.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which average is most affected by extreme outliers?
options: mean
median
mode
range

mcqs.q: When solving 3x = 12, what do you do to both sides?
options: Subtract 3 from both sides because 3 was multiplying x.
Strong correlation means the variables are equal in value.
Divide both sides by 3 to get x = 4.
Multiply both sides by 3 to undo the equation.

mcqs.q: What is the range of the data set [4, 7, 2, 9, 5]?
options: Strong correlation means the variables are equal in value.
7 — the largest minus the smallest (9 - 2).
5, because that is the middle value.
From 2 to 9 — the range is given as two values.

mcqs.q: If two variables are strongly correlated, what can you conclude?
options: They vary together — but correlation alone does not establish that one causes the other.
Strong correlation means that one variable causes the other.
Strong correlation means the variables are equal in value.
5, because that is the middle value.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Cumulative frequency”?
options: Mean = sum/n. Median = middle value of ordered data. Mode = most frequent value. Different averages, different uses.
Values far from the rest. Common rule: outside Q₁ − 1.5·IQR or Q₃ + 1.5·IQR. May skew mean.
Running total. Plotting against upper class boundary gives an S-curve, used to estimate medians and quartiles.
Range = max − min. IQR = Q₃ − Q₁ (middle 50% spread). Standard deviation σ = √(variance), more sensitive measure.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Range, IQR, SD”?
options: Values far from the rest. Common rule: outside Q₁ − 1.5·IQR or Q₃ + 1.5·IQR. May skew mean.
Show min, Q₁, median, Q₃, max. Visualise spread, skew, outliers. Useful for comparing distributions.
Random, stratified, systematic, opportunity, quota. Aim: representative of population without bias.
Range = max − min. IQR = Q₃ − Q₁ (middle 50% spread). Standard deviation σ = √(variance), more sensitive measure.
